claim: Neurotransmitter release requires formation of trans-SNARE complexes between the synaptic vesicle and plasma membranes.
source: Neurotransmitter release requires formation of trans-SNARE complexes between the synaptic vesicle and plasma membranes, which likely underlies synaptic vesicle priming to a release-ready state.
evidence: This is a statement from the abstract that reflects established scientific understanding in the field.

claim: Trans-SNARE complex formation likely underlies synaptic vesicle priming to a release-ready state.
source: Neurotransmitter release requires formation of trans-SNARE complexes between the synaptic vesicle and plasma membranes, which likely underlies synaptic vesicle priming to a release-ready state.
evidence: This is a speculative statement indicated by 'likely' in the abstract.

claim: Trans-SNARE complex formation in the presence of NSF-αSNAP requires both Munc18-1 and Munc13-1.
source: Here we show that trans-SNARE complex formation in the presence of NSF-αSNAP requires both Munc18-1 and Munc13-1, as proposed previously, and is facilitated by synaptotagmin-1.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study presented in the manuscript, supported by experimental data shown in Figures 3 and 4.

claim: Trans-SNARE complex formation in the presence of NSF-αSNAP is facilitated by synaptotagmin-1.
source: Here we show that trans-SNARE complex formation in the presence of NSF-αSNAP requires both Munc18-1 and Munc13-1, as proposed previously, and is facilitated by synaptotagmin-1.
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data in the manuscript.

claim: Munc18-1, Munc13-1, complexin-1 and likely synaptotagmin-1 contribute to maintaining assembled trans-SNARE complexes in the presence of NSF-αSNAP.
source: Our data also show that Munc18-1, Munc13-1, complexin-1 and likely synaptotagmin-1 contribute to maintaining assembled trans-SNARE complexes in the presence of NSF-αSNAP.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in Figures 3-5.

claim: Munc18-1 and Munc13-1 are critical for mediating vesicle priming.
source: We propose a model whereby Munc18-1 and Munc13-1 are critical not only for mediating vesicle priming but also for precluding de-priming by preventing trans-SNARE complex disassembly
evidence: This is part of the proposed model based on the experimental findings and prior knowledge.

claim: Munc18-1 and Munc13-1 preclude de-priming by preventing trans-SNARE complex disassembly.
source: We propose a model whereby Munc18-1 and Munc13-1 are critical not only for mediating vesicle priming but also for precluding de-priming by preventing trans-SNARE complex disassembly
evidence: This is part of the proposed model based on experimental findings shown in Figures 3-5.

claim: Complexin-1 impairs de-priming.
source: in this model, complexin-1 also impairs de-priming, while synaptotagmin-1 may assist in priming and hinder de-priming.
evidence: This is part of the proposed model based on experimental findings shown in Figures 3-5.

claim: Synaptotagmin-1 may assist in priming.
source: in this model, complexin-1 also impairs de-priming, while synaptotagmin-1 may assist in priming and hinder de-priming.
evidence: This is a speculative statement indicated by 'may' in the abstract, based on experimental observations.

claim: Synaptotagmin-1 may hinder de-priming.
source: in this model, complexin-1 also impairs de-priming, while synaptotagmin-1 may assist in priming and hinder de-priming.
evidence: This is a speculative statement indicated by 'may' in the abstract, based on experimental observations.

claim: SNAREs synaptobrevin, syntaxin-1 and SNAP-25 form a parallel four-helix bundle called the SNARE complex.
source: The soluble N-ethylmaleimide sensitive factor attachment protein receptors (SNAREs) synaptobrevin, syntaxin-1 and SNAP-25 form a parallel four-helix bundle called the SNARE complex that brings the synaptic vesicle and plasma membranes together and is key for membrane fusion (Hanson et al., 1997; Poirier et al., 1998; Söllner et al., 1993; Sutton et al., 1998).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: The SNARE complex brings the synaptic vesicle and plasma membranes together and is key for membrane fusion.
source: The soluble N-ethylmaleimide sensitive factor attachment protein receptors (SNAREs) synaptobrevin, syntaxin-1 and SNAP-25 form a parallel four-helix bundle called the SNARE complex that brings the synaptic vesicle and plasma membranes together and is key for membrane fusion (Hanson et al., 1997; Poirier et al., 1998; Söllner et al., 1993; Sutton et al., 1998).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: NSF and SNAPs disassemble SNARE complexes after release to recycle the SNAREs for another round of fusion.
source: N-ethylmaleimide sensitive factor (NSF) and soluble NSF attachment proteins (SNAPs; no relation to SNAP-25) disassemble SNARE complexes after release to recycle the SNAREs for another round of fusion (Banerjee et al., 1996; Mayer et al., 1996; Söllner et al., 1993).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Munc18-1 and Munc13s orchestrate SNARE complex assembly in an NSF-SNAP-resistant manner.
source: Munc18-1 and Munc13s orchestrate SNARE complex assembly in an NSF-SNAP-resistant manner (Ma et al., 2013) that improves the fidelity of parallel assembly (Lai et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Munc18-1 and Munc13s improve the fidelity of parallel SNARE complex assembly.
source: Munc18-1 and Munc13s orchestrate SNARE complex assembly in an NSF-SNAP-resistant manner (Ma et al., 2013) that improves the fidelity of parallel assembly (Lai et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Munc18-1 binds to a self-inhibited 'closed conformation' of syntaxin-1.
source: The underlying mechanism involves binding of Munc18-1 to a self-inhibited 'closed conformation' of syntaxin-1 (Dulubova et al., 1999; Misura et al., 2000) and to synaptobrevin, thus forming a template to assemble the SNARE complex (Baker et al., 2015; Parisotto et al., 2014; Sitarska et al., 2017)
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Munc18-1 binds to synaptobrevin, forming a template to assemble the SNARE complex.
source: The underlying mechanism involves binding of Munc18-1 to a self-inhibited 'closed conformation' of syntaxin-1 (Dulubova et al., 1999; Misura et al., 2000) and to synaptobrevin, thus forming a template to assemble the SNARE complex (Baker et al., 2015; Parisotto et al., 2014; Sitarska et al., 2017)
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Munc13s bridge the vesicle and plasma membranes.
source: while Munc13s bridge the vesicle and plasma membranes (Liu et al., 2016) and help to open syntaxin-1 (Ma et al., 2011; Richmond et al., 2001; Yang et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Munc13s help to open syntaxin-1.
source: while Munc13s bridge the vesicle and plasma membranes (Liu et al., 2016) and help to open syntaxin-1 (Ma et al., 2011; Richmond et al., 2001; Yang et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Synaptotagmin-1 acts as the major Ca2+ sensor that triggers release through interactions with phospholipids and the SNARE complex.
source: Synaptotagmin-1 acts as the major Ca2+ sensor that triggers release through interactions with phospholipids (Fernández-Chacón et al., 2001) and the SNARE complex (Brewer et al., 2015; Zhou et al., 2015; Zhou et al., 2017), in a tight interplay with complexins (Giraudo et al., 2006; Schaub et al., 2006; Tang et al., 2006).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The primed state is believed to include trans-SNARE complexes that are partially formed, with the N-terminal half assembled and at least part of the C-terminal, membrane proximal portion unassembled.
source: The primed state is believed to include trans-SNARE complexes that are partially formed, with the N-terminal half assembled and at least part of the C-terminal, membrane proximal portion unassembled (e.g. Sørensen et al., 2006; Walter et al., 2010)
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research and represents current understanding in the field.

claim: NSF-αSNAP disassemble not only cis-SNARE complexes but also syntaxin-1-SNAP-25 heterodimers.
source: This interpretation arose in part because NSF-αSNAP disassemble not only cis-SNARE complexes but also syntaxin-1-SNAP-25 heterodimers (Hayashi et al., 1995)
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: The NSF-αSNAP homologues Sec18-Sec17 disassemble trans-SNARE complexes in yeast vacuolar fusion.
source: However, studies of yeast vacuolar fusion showed that the NSF-αSNAP homologues Sec18-Sec17 disassemble trans-SNARE complexes and that disassembly is prevented by HOPS, a tethering complex that includes the Munc18-1 homologue Vps33 and coordinates SNARE complex formation (Mima et al., 2008; Xu et al., 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Disassembly of trans-SNARE complexes by Sec18-Sec17 is prevented by HOPS in yeast vacuolar fusion.
source: However, studies of yeast vacuolar fusion showed that the NSF-αSNAP homologues Sec18-Sec17 disassemble trans-SNARE complexes and that disassembly is prevented by HOPS, a tethering complex that includes the Munc18-1 homologue Vps33 and coordinates SNARE complex formation (Mima et al., 2008; Xu et al., 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: At least a fraction of neuronal trans-SNARE complexes can be disassembled by NSF-αSNAP in vitro.
source: Moreover, recent reports showed that at least a fraction of neuronal trans-SNARE complexes can be disassembled by NSF-αSNAP in vitro (Yavuz et al., 2018)
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Munc18-1 and Munc13-1 are critical to prevent de-priming of readily-releasable synaptic vesicles in neurons.
source: and that Munc18-1 and Munc13-1 are critical to prevent de-priming of readily-releasable synaptic vesicles in neurons, but such requirement can be bypassed by the NSF inactivating agent N-ethylmaleimide (He et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: The requirement for Munc18-1 and Munc13-1 to prevent de-priming can be bypassed by N-ethylmaleimide.
source: and that Munc18-1 and Munc13-1 are critical to prevent de-priming of readily-releasable synaptic vesicles in neurons, but such requirement can be bypassed by the NSF inactivating agent N-ethylmaleimide (He et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Deletion of synaptotagmin-1 leads to decreases in the RRP of vesicles.
source: subsequent analyses revealed that absence of these proteins does decrease the RRP of vesicles (Bacaj et al., 2015; Chang et al., 2018; Xue et al., 2010; Yang et al., 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Deletion of complexins leads to decreases in the RRP of vesicles.
source: subsequent analyses revealed that absence of these proteins does decrease the RRP of vesicles (Bacaj et al., 2015; Chang et al., 2018; Xue et al., 2010; Yang et al., 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The SNAP-25 M71D,L78D mutation prevents membrane fusion in reconstitution assays.
source: content mixing was abolished and lipid mixing was very inefficient when SNAP-25m was used in the assays instead of WT SNAP-25 (Figure 1B,C), demonstrating that the M71D,L78D mutation in SNAP-25 indeed prevents membrane fusion.
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B,C.

claim: NSF-αSNAP disassembled about 50% of pre-formed trans-SNARE complexes.
source: These results show that NSF-αSNAP disassembled a fraction of the trans-SNARE complexes (estimated to be about 50%) while the remaining complexes were resistant to NSF-αSNAP
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: A fraction of trans-SNARE complexes remained resistant to NSF-αSNAP disassembly.
source: These results show that NSF-αSNAP disassembled a fraction of the trans-SNARE complexes (estimated to be about 50%) while the remaining complexes were resistant to NSF-αSNAP, in agreement with the results of Yavuz et al. (2018).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B and corroborated by prior research.

claim: Disassembly of trans-SNARE complexes required ATP hydrolysis by NSF.
source: Disassembly of trans-SNARE complexes required ATP hydrolysis by NSF, as no disassembly was observed when Mg2+ was replaced by EDTA in the reaction, or NSF was bound to ATPγS rather than ATP (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The αSNAP K122E,K163E mutation strongly impaired trans-SNARE complex disassembly.
source: Both αSNAP mutations strongly impaired the recovery of donor fluorescence observed when trans-SNARE complexes were disassembled by NSF in the presence of wild type (WT) αSNAP (compare green and red curves in Figure 2D,E)
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D,E.

claim: The αSNAP F27S,F28S mutation strongly impaired trans-SNARE complex disassembly.
source: Both αSNAP mutations strongly impaired the recovery of donor fluorescence observed when trans-SNARE complexes were disassembled by NSF in the presence of wild type (WT) αSNAP (compare green and red curves in Figure 2D,E)
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D,E.

claim: Interactions of αSNAP with both the membranes and the SNAREs are critical for trans-SNARE complex disassembly.
source: showing that interactions of αSNAP with both the membranes and the SNAREs are critical for trans-SNARE complex disassembly.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data shown in Figure 2D,E.

claim: Complexin-1 and synaptotagmin-1 C2AB were unable to support trans-SNARE complex assembly in the presence of NSF-αSNAP.
source: Complexin-1 and synaptotagmin-1 C2AB were unable to support trans-SNARE complex assembly in the presence of NSF-αSNAP even after Ca2+ addition, and did not appear to enhance the rate of trans-SNARE complex assembly supported by Munc18-1 and Munc13-1 C1C2BMUNC2C (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Complexin-1 completely prevented disassembly of trans-SNARE complexes upon addition of EGTA.
source: Including complexin-1 completely prevented such disassembly, whereas synaptotagmin-1 C2AB had no effect (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Synaptotagmin-1 C2AB had no effect on preventing disassembly of trans-SNARE complexes upon addition of EGTA.
source: Including complexin-1 completely prevented such disassembly, whereas synaptotagmin-1 C2AB had no effect (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Membrane-anchored synaptotagmin-1 facilitates NSF-αSNAP-resistant assembly mediated by Munc18-1 and Munc13-1 C1C2BMUNC2C.
source: Ca2+-independent assembly was more efficient with the VSyt1-liposomes than with V-liposomes, suggesting that membrane-anchored synaptotagmin-1 facilitates the NSF-αSNAP-resistant assembly mediated by Munc18-1 and Munc13-1 C1C2BMUNC2C.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from experimental data comparing results with V-liposomes and VSyt1-liposomes.

claim: Membrane-anchored synaptotagmin-1 helps to protect trans-SNARE complexes against disassembly by NSF-αSNAP once they are formed.
source: These results indicate that membrane-anchored synaptotagmin-1 may help to protect trans-SNARE complexes against disassembly by NSF-αSNAP once they are formed.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from experimental data shown in Figure 3F.

claim: Complexin-1 partially inhibits assembly of trans-SNARE complexes between VSyt1- and T-liposomes in the absence of Ca2+.
source: These results suggest that, in the absence of Ca2+, complexin-1 partially inhibits assembly of trans-SNARE complexes between VSyt1- and T-liposomes but increases the overall assembly efficiency because it protects trans-SNARE complexes against disassembly by NSF-αSNAP
evidence: This is an inference drawn from experimental data shown in Figure 3E and Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Complexin-1 increases the overall assembly efficiency of trans-SNARE complexes because it protects against disassembly by NSF-αSNAP.
source: These results suggest that, in the absence of Ca2+, complexin-1 partially inhibits assembly of trans-SNARE complexes between VSyt1- and T-liposomes but increases the overall assembly efficiency because it protects trans-SNARE complexes against disassembly by NSF-αSNAP
evidence: This is an inference drawn from experimental data shown in Figure 3E and Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Ca2+-bound synaptotagmin-1 C2AB markedly protected trans-SNARE complexes against disassembly.
source: However, assembly was dramatically accelerated by C2AB in the presence of Ca2+ (Figure 4A, blue curve), likely because C2AB can bridge two membranes together (Araç et al., 2006), and addition of NSF-αSNAP led to only a small amount of donor fluorescence recovery, suggesting that Ca2+-bound C2AB markedly protected trans-SNARE complexes against disassembly (but see below).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Complexin-1 accelerated trans-SNARE complex assembly.
source: Complexin-1 accelerated trans-SNARE complex assembly (Figure 4A, red curve), consistent with previous results (Diao et al., 2013), and appeared to partially prevent disassembly by NSF-αSNAP.
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A and corroborated by prior research.

claim: Complexin-1 appeared to partially prevent disassembly of trans-SNARE complexes by NSF-αSNAP.
source: Complexin-1 accelerated trans-SNARE complex assembly (Figure 4A, red curve), consistent with previous results (Diao et al., 2013), and appeared to partially prevent disassembly by NSF-αSNAP.
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Munc18-1 and Munc13-1 C1C2BMUNC2C cooperate with NSF-αSNAP in formation of trans-SNARE complexes.
source: Addition of NSF-αSNAP consistently led to a slight further decrease in donor fluorescence intensity (Figure 4B, red curve), supporting the notion that Munc18-1 and Munc13-1 C1C2BMUNC2C protect against trans-SNARE complex disassembly by NSF-αSNAP, and suggesting that they in fact cooperate with NSF-αSNAP in formation of trans-SNARE complexes.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from experimental data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Synaptotagmin-1 by itself does not protect against disassembly of trans-SNARE complexes.
source: We observed similar rates of assembly and similar amounts of disassembly in the absence and presence of Ca2+ (Figure 4C), which indicates that synaptotagmin-1 by itself does not protect against disassembly
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Complexin-1 strongly hindered disassembly of trans-SNARE complexes by NSF-αSNAP.
source: Including complexin-1 decreased the assembly rate but enhanced the overall efficiency of assembly and strongly hindered disassembly of trans-SNARE complexes by NSF-αSNAP (Figure 4C, red curve)
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Munc18-1 and Munc13-1 C1C2BMUNC2C synergistically help to maintain assembled trans-SNARE complexes in the presence of NSF-αSNAP.
source: Moreover, we find that Munc18-1 and Munc13-1 synergistically help to maintain assembled trans-SNARE complexes in the presence of NSF-αSNAP, which is strongly enhanced by Ca2+
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in Figures 3-5.

claim: Ca2+ strongly enhances the ability of Munc18-1 and Munc13-1 to maintain assembled trans-SNARE complexes in the presence of NSF-αSNAP.
source: Moreover, we find that Munc18-1 and Munc13-1 synergistically help to maintain assembled trans-SNARE complexes in the presence of NSF-αSNAP, which is strongly enhanced by Ca2+
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in Figures 3-5.

claim: Trans-SNARE complexes are protected against disassembly by complexin-1.
source: and that trans-SNARE complexes are protected against disassembly by complexin-1.
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in Figures 3-5.

claim: Munc18-1 and Munc13-1 C1C2BMUNC2C were unable to support cis-SNARE complex assembly even after addition of Ca2+.
source: Munc18-1 and the Munc13-1 C1C2BMUNC2C fragment were unable to support cis-SNARE complex assembly even after addition of Ca2+ (Figure 6C, red curve)
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Munc18-1 and Munc13-1 C1C2BMUNC2C partially inhibited cis-SNARE complex assembly catalyzed by Syb49-93.
source: and they partially inhibited cis-SNARE complex assembly catalyzed by Syb49-93, without protecting against disassembly upon addition of NSF-αSNAP (Figure 6C, gray curve).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Munc18-1 and Munc13-1 C1C2BMUNC2C did not protect cis-SNARE complexes against disassembly by NSF-αSNAP.
source: and they partially inhibited cis-SNARE complex assembly catalyzed by Syb49-93, without protecting against disassembly upon addition of NSF-αSNAP (Figure 6C, gray curve).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: The apposition of two membranes tilts the balance in favor of SNARE complex assembly.
source: Overall, the contrast of the results obtained with cis-SNARE complexes with those observed with trans-SNARE complexes provides a dramatic demonstration of how the apposition of two membranes tilts the balance in favor of SNARE complex assembly, whereas disassembly dominates on a single membrane.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from comparing experimental results with cis- and trans-SNARE complexes shown in Figures 3-6.

claim: Disassembly dominates on a single membrane.
source: Overall, the contrast of the results obtained with cis-SNARE complexes with those observed with trans-SNARE complexes provides a dramatic demonstration of how the apposition of two membranes tilts the balance in favor of SNARE complex assembly, whereas disassembly dominates on a single membrane.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from comparing experimental results with cis- and trans-SNARE complexes shown in Figures 3-6.

claim: Ca2+-binding to the Munc13-1 C2B domain brings the two membranes into closer proximity.
source: Moreover, Ca2+-binding to the Munc13-1 C2B domain is expected to change the orientation of Munc13-1 C1C2BMUNC2C with respect to the plasma membrane, bringing the two membranes into closer proximity (Xu et al., 2017)
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Ca2+-binding to the Munc13-1 C2B domain potentially increases steric constraints that impair 20S complex assembly.
source: and potentially increasing the steric constraints that impair 20S complex assembly.
evidence: This is a speculative statement based on inference from structural considerations.

claim: The core of the primed state is formed by a macromolecular assembly that includes trans-SNARE complexes, Munc18-1, Munc13-1, complexin-1 and synaptotagmin-1.
source: Based on the available data, we propose that the core of this primed state is formed by a macromolecular assembly that includes trans-SNARE complexes, Munc18-1, Munc13-1, complexin-1 and synaptotagmin-1.
evidence: This is a proposed model based on the experimental findings from the study.
